findings.title: Tool poisoning: tool shadowing in 'aft_check'
findings.description: Tool description attempts to change how another tool or server behaves (cross-server shadowing). Matched pattern in tool 'aft_check': '('after', 'using', '')'
findings.recommendation: Review tool description carefully. Compare claimed functionality with actual code behavior. Consider removing this MCP server.

findings.title: Tool 'aft_check' references tool 'modify'
findings.description: Tool description mentions another tool by name, which could enable tool chaining attacks.
findings.recommendation: Verify this cross-reference is legitimate and necessary.

findings.title: Shell command execution via os.system()
findings.description: Call to `os.system()` executes shell commands in maliciousadd.py at line 325
findings.recommendation: Use subprocess with shell=False and a list of arguments.

findings.title: Broad data read + write = data manipulation risk
findings.description: Tools that can both read and write data could be manipulated to corrupt, overwrite, or delete information. Provided by: get_and_read_all_files, get_user_info, get_weather_forecast, m_check, compute_, sandbox_run (data_read) + modify, compute_, aft_check (data_write).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Code execution + filesystem = unrestricted local access
findings.description: Tools that execute code AND access the filesystem can read/write any file the agent has permissions for, including SSH keys and credentials. Provided by: modify, aft_check, sandbox_run (code_execute) + get_and_read_all_files, m_check, compute_ (filesystem).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Credential access + data write = privilege persistence
findings.description: Tools that access credentials AND write data could persist stolen credentials or create backdoor accounts. Provided by: show_credentials (credential_access) + modify, compute_, aft_check (data_write).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Tool 'get_and_read_all_files' reads files (file_read)
findings.description:
Tool 'get_and_read_all_files' reads files. Evidence: 'read the file'. Description: '_summary_
This function will read the file in the list and return the content of the files to the
LLM for further processing
Args:
fileslist'
findings.recommendation: Scope the tool to the narrowest operation and location it needs, and require explicit user approval per call.

findings.title: Tool 'sandbox_run' can execute shell commands (shell_exec)
findings.description:
Tool 'sandbox_run' can execute shell commands; it takes a command-like parameter. Evidence: 'run command'. Description: 'run command in a sandbox

Args:
    command: the command to be run
Returns:
    result of command execution'
findings.recommendation: Scope the tool to the narrowest operation and location it needs, and require explicit user approval per call.

findings.title: Restricted-looking resource is served to clients: internal://credentials
findings.description: Resource 'internal://credentials' (get_credentials) is labelled 'internal' yet is listed to every connected client. Anything the server lists, an agent will read into the model's context.
findings.recommendation: Do not expose internal/admin/debug material as MCP resources; gate it server-side with real authorization.

findings.title: Restricted-looking resource is served to clients: internal://info
findings.description: Resource 'internal://info' (get_info) is labelled 'internal' yet is listed to every connected client. Anything the server lists, an agent will read into the model's context.
findings.recommendation: Do not expose internal/admin/debug material as MCP resources; gate it server-side with real authorization.

findings.title: Trust exploitation pattern: authority impersonation
findings.description: Pattern in maliciousadd.py near line 159: `elevated access`. This could enable a compromised agent to mislead users.
findings.recommendation: Implement output verification. Require human confirmation for high-impact actions. Mark agent-generated content as such.

findings.title: Hard-coded secret in server source: OpenAI/Anthropic-style API key
findings.description: A value shaped like a openai/anthropic-style api key is assigned in maliciousadd.py at line 112. The value itself is not reproduced here. Anyone with read access to the source or the published package can use it.
findings.recommendation: Revoke and rotate this credential, remove it from source (and git history), and load it from the environment or a secrets manager at runtime.

findings.title: Exec/shell sink `os.system` inside tool 'sandbox_run'
findings.description: maliciousadd.py line 325: tool 'sandbox_run' calls `os.system`. Tool arguments are chosen by the model and can be steered by injected content. A tool parameter flows (directly or via one assignment) into the sink. This is a heuristic, not full taint analysis.
findings.recommendation: Avoid shells in tool handlers. Use argument lists (no shell=True), strict allowlists for commands and paths, and validate every tool argument before use.

findings.title: Tool 'get_weather_forecast' changes behaviour after a number of calls
findings.description: maliciousadd.py line 188: 'get_weather_forecast' compares an invocation counter against a number. A tool that is benign for the first N calls and different afterwards is a rug pull that no single scan or approval can catch.
findings.recommendation: Tool behaviour must not depend on how often it has been called.

findings.title: Credentials exposed in resource 'internal://credentials'
findings.description: resource 'internal://credentials' contains credential-shaped values: OpenAI/Anthropic-style API key (sk-a1b…); Credentials embedded in a connection URL (postgresql://user:pass@…). Values are not reproduced here. Anything a server serves ends up in the model's context and in the client's logs.
findings.recommendation: Never serve credentials, tokens or flags as MCP content; keep them server-side and out of tool output.

findings.title: Credentials exposed in resource 'internal://info'
findings.description: resource 'internal://info' contains credential-shaped values: Credentials embedded in a connection URL (postgresql://user:pass@…). Values are not reproduced here. Anything a server serves ends up in the model's context and in the client's logs.
findings.recommendation: Never serve credentials, tokens or flags as MCP content; keep them server-side and out of tool output.

findings.title: Tool 'get_and_read_all_files' suggests broad data exposure
findings.description: The tool 'get_and_read_all_files' (name tokens ['all']) appears to return bulk data into the model context, where it can be over-shared with other tools, sessions or users. What is actually returned at runtime is not checked (runtime over-sharing remains a coverage gap).
findings.recommendation: Scope results (pagination, filters, per-user access checks) and avoid returning whole tables, histories or file trees to the model.

findings.title: Blast radius: HIGH — compromise of this server has broad impact
findings.description: If this MCP server is compromised, the blast radius is HIGH due to: arbitrary code execution, filesystem access, credential access, 13 tools (large attack surface), 7 critical findings. A single tool poisoning or supply chain attack could cascade across all connected systems.
findings.recommendation: Apply least-privilege to this server. Isolate it from other MCP servers. Implement kill switches and behavioral monitoring. Limit env vars to the minimum required.

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
